_comment: tools/profile.sh ARMS ARM SIZE BENCH OUT. Paths are the host's; every arm names what it measures (commit, SDK, compiler) so a number is traceable. share must contain spec_root and every OUT.

platform._note: cpu_props are the module build's needs: dev's default (paged table) module reads the test CSRs, which QEMU a9936e7037 makes illegal unless asked for; the plain arm boots the same module

cap-dev.note: dev's default module build (paged table), SDK defaults

rv64.note: the plain image executes from the share, which therefore keeps the host's permissions

cap-dev-perlbench.label: cap-dev
cap-dev-perlbench.commit: llvm-capstone b9dd0ccc0b31 (dev 2026-11-02), SDK defaults: heap_lifetimes on, heap_scrub_free off
cap-dev-perlbench.note: 500.perlbench_r: test.pl runs each of its 317 scripts as a child domain and waits for it; with one supervisor slot (QEMU's and the module's default) the waiting parent holds the slot and the child sleeps in vm_ioctl for it forever, so the arm needs two (QEMU property and module parameter)

rv64-perlbench.label: rv64
rv64-perlbench.commit: llvm-capstone b9dd0ccc0b31, RISCV target, musl 1.2.5 pristine
rv64-perlbench.note: 500.perlbench_r: t/op/stat.t test 33 (-o) needs the files the guest's root creates in the run directory to be root's, which share_model none does not give; the staged image does not run from the share
